comments.text:
Really good video that sums up almost everything happening here. However, it missed a couple of points that connect Ecuador's current situation:
     - Correa took the police and military out of the penitentiary system leaving "prison guides" as the only entity to look over the prisons. This ended up creating more corruption, since most of the guides were on the cartels' payrolls, and the ones who were not were threatened or killed if they did not comply.
     - Correa gave power to lots of criminal organizations when they were still local gangs back in 2008, signing peace deals and even giving them a voice in the Assembly, which gave them access to political power.

     - As the left in Ecuador was deeply interconnected with the gangs, when the people finally opened their eyes and voted the left out of power, these groups started causing terror—killing people and launching all kinds of attacks on citizens and non-left political figures. This made uneducated people say, "We were better off under Correa (left wing),"pushing them toward wanting to return to socialism—the end goal—to get back to that peaceful time when drugs and other illicit activities happened without opposition.

     - The school system is the backbone of all this craziness. Socialist idealism is promoted, drugs are dealt in schools, and poor, insufficient curricula are used. This makes lower-class kids in Ecuador living in poverty look for another way out, 5 times out of 10 choosing to join these organizations where they are trained to kill and do many other things for what they think is quick, "good, and easy money."

There is quite a lot more going on. Thanks for sharing with the world what's happening here—I wish more people could understand this.
